license.changes: The HTML is retained unchanged. Decoded text is not trimmed, normalized or corrected. Two leading newline characters before selected 453 require an explicit structural classification. This intake adds no English translation.

source.note: This exact retrieval is pinned in addition to its revision ID. The candidate inventory has 108 rendered headings and 157 numbered markers. Structural coverage is not a claim that every printed heading or narration variant is present. Edition identity and wording approval are not inferred.

findings: Two newline characters before selected 453 are retained as a separate blank span. Both printed witnesses show a distinct new chain there and an untitled chapter 79 which the digital source omits. This whole-book structural inventory does not admit the later report or silently insert its missing heading.

Selected 342 spans Bewley 342 and the first account under 343. The second unnumbered account under 343 is selected 343. Explicit part scopes preserve all selected segment ownership and reject lost, repeated or unordered shared parts.

Both full source chains and embedded attributions remain at 342, including the attribution omitted from the Khan-family body. The selected sixth heaven, return verb and pearl wording are unchanged; provisional English lexical choices and print differences are documented with commentary references.

Selected 344 retains its closing transmission even though the inspected modern print and Khan-family body omit it. Its source garment term and supplication wording are retained without importing the comparison’s different terminology.

The four unnumbered introductions are individually browsable Arabic, excluded from sessions and narration. English remains pending. The comparison’s separate Clothing in the Prayer section does not create a new source book.
Ten individually matched Khan-family comparison records are pinned to their source and record hashes: 1.8.345 through 1.8.354. This is a checked local mapping, not a full-book numbering offset.

All twelve selected Arabic reports are unchanged. Historical print PDF pages 102–105 and modern print PDF pages 101–103 were visually inspected. The modern print numbers these bodies 359–370; selected references remain 352–363.

353 retains uncertainty between hearing and asking, and Abu Hurayrah’s testimony. The abbreviated English comparisons do not replace its complete chain. Fath al-Bari identifies the uncertain transmission as Yahya reporting from Ikrimah.

354 retains we asked and the night-time question, plus the narrator explanation that the garment was narrow. 355 retains the selected passive the women were told instead of adding a named speaker from an English comparison.

358 retains eight stated clothing pairs and a ninth uncertain pair in order, with Umar’s statement distinguished from the Prophetic answer. Source garment terms remain explicit; explanatory notes stay outside the quotation.

359 retains the closing Nafi chain present in both prints and Bewley but absent from the matched Khan-family EPUB body. 360–361 preserve source terminology without importing competing detailed glosses as hadith wording.
362 retains the intervening Humayd attribution, Abu Hurayrah’s return and both full proclamations. 363 retains we said and Abu Abd Allah rather than the comparison’s I said and Abdullah.

The chapter 7 introduction is separately browsable Arabic, with English pending. It never enters numbered sessions or narration. Twelve Khan-family bodies were individually matched to 1.8.355–1.8.366 and hash-bound; this is not an assumed full-book offset.

All fourteen selected Arabic reports remain unchanged. Historical print PDF pages 105–109 and modern print PDF pages 104–107 were visually inspected for the numbered reports; modern page 103 also supplies the chapter 12 introduction. The modern print numbers these report bodies 371–384; selected references remain 364–377.

364 preserves the active uncovering wording, full Abd al-Aziz interjection, source garment and food terms, complete marriage and feast account, and uncertainty about sawiq. 365 does not import a darkness explanation from other reports. 366 preserves a single selected entry and both transmissions while explicitly mapping comparison parts to Khan-family 1.8.369 and 1.8.370.

367 retains the selected female subject rather than the English comparison’s he. 368 does not add an unnamed giver or reason for removal. 369 retains Awn from his father, two rakahs, and the selected position relative to the spear, despite shortened comparison wording.

370 keeps backward stepping and does not import a second recitation from the historical print and an English comparison. Its full closing compiler/transmitter discussion is a visible Transmission note, including the final question and No answer. The mercy honorific uses smaller presentation spans while all canonical and narration text remains complete.

371 retains the leg-or-shoulder uncertainty and tree trunks without adding a species or importing a different sitting instruction. 373 retains his grandmother because the pronoun’s referent is disputed in Fath al-Bari, our mat, sprinkling and unnamed participants. 375–377 retain the full relationships, speaker perspectives, bed comparison and selected chain endings.

All eleven added chapter headings and five Arabic introductions remain separately browsable offline. Introduction English is pending. Chapter material never enters numbered sessions or narration. Fifteen Khan-family bodies were individually matched to fourteen selected reports and hash-bound; references are not assigned using an assumed global offset.

All fifteen selected Arabic reports remain unchanged. Historical print PDF pages 109–113 and modern print PDF pages 107–110 were visually inspected. The modern print groups these bodies under 385–401, including two printed reports within selected 385 and two within selected 387. Selected references remain 378–392.

378 keeps the singular one of us. 379 retains Abu Maslamah Sa’id ibn Yazid as one person. 380 preserves Ibrahim’s closing note and does not add the wet-hands explanation. 381 and 383 map individually to the literal English labels 1.8.385l and 1.8.385u, including their suffix letters.

382 has no corresponding report between those adjacent suffixed EPUB records. The reader discloses the local gap, one completed English translation-family comparison and a supplementary modern reference at Sunnah.com Bukhari 389. Its deprecated 1.8.385 label is not an EPUB record. This is absence from the checked sequence, not a claim that every occurrence elsewhere in the collection was searched. The uncertainty in its closing statement is retained.

The comparison validator now checks adjacency in actual pinned EPUB record order and requires exact record evidence for suffixed absence boundaries. It rejects invented, reversed or nonadjacent boundaries and missing or altered evidence rather than applying decimal arithmetic to edition labels.

383 retains al-Layth’s closing transmission. 384 keeps protection wording without an inserted legal interpretation. 385 preserves all three chains and both narration bodies, including the middle chain omitted from the English EPUB, and distinguishes slaughter as we slaughter from eat what we slaughter. 386 retains east then west and the complete closing chain.

387 retains both We asked introductions and the closing Jabir report despite a different modern printed division. 388 retains both references to two rakahs and the selected door wording; 389 retains the differing account of prayer outside the Ka’bah without harmonization. 390 retains sixteen-or-seventeen uncertainty and third-person testimony. 391 adds no optional-prayer gloss. 392 keeps Ibrahim’s uncertainty between the opening and resumed report, without importing the five-prayer-unit account from a different report.

All nine chapter headings and four Arabic introductions remain separately browsable offline. English introductions remain pending; they never enter numbered sessions or narration. The complete dual honorific may Allah Most High be pleased with them both now uses one smaller presentation span, including earlier entries 8, 10 and 12, without changing stored text or narration scripts.

Prayer 393–407 adds fifteen complete numbered source entries and eight complete chapters (32–39). Fourteen Arabic reports remain unchanged. Entry 401 has one declared final-letter correction, ولا عن يمينة to ولا عن يمينه, supported by both inspected Arabic prints; the original full digital report remains accessible offline.

Historical print PDF pages 113–116 and modern print PDF pages 111–113 were visually inspected. The modern print groups these entries under 402–417: 394 is an additional chain under 402, while selected 400 combines modern 408–409 and selected 401 combines 410–411. These are recorded edition-specific groupings, not a universal number offset.

Every English comparison body was individually read: Bewley 393–407 and the pinned Khan-family EPUB 1.8.395–1.8.409. The latter contains only Narrated Anas: and as above (395). for selected 394. Both the exact pointer body and its earlier target record are hash-bound. No preceding narration is silently copied into the selected chain-only entry.

394 keeps its complete abbreviated chain visible and supplies a separate backward link to 393. 393 retains I agreed with my Lord and its full three matters; 395 keeps the imperative, unnamed visitor, morning and tonight wording. 396 keeps the plural reply and two prostrations without importing uncertainty from 392.

The digital chapter 34 omits an Ibn Abbas quotation present in both Arabic prints. A separate, evidence-bound printed-introduction record preserves both readings, exact pages and transcription policy without changing the digital chapter blocks. The one original digital introduction in chapter 32 and this printed quotation remain Arabic with English pending, outside numbered daily sessions and narration.

397 keeps the selected plural feet and explicit or uncertainty; the prints have a singular foot. 399 retains its three lexical alternatives. 400 keeps both narrators and one pebble. 401 preserves both honorifics and its distinct informed-him wording. 402–403 receive no extra left-foot qualification from another witness or heading.

404 retains the closing al-Zuhri/Humayd transmission omitted from the English EPUB and does not substitute Abu Hurayrah. 405 keeps the unqualified sin/expiation statement. 406 preserves place-of-prayer wording, without adding an angel identity or witness-only honorific. 407 preserves both uncertainties and the complete garment demonstration. Primary commentary locators 423, 425, 427–429 inform comparison notes without importing commentary into the narration.

Printed chapter material is validated at intake and in the reader catalog. Invalid placement, stale source/reading evidence, missing second witnesses, unreviewed English, invented approval and inconsistent paragraph metadata are rejected. The printed quotation has separate attribution in the source record and never enters report text or speech scripts.

Prayer 408–424 adds seventeen complete numbered reports, forty-six English segments and fifteen complete source chapters (40–54). Sixteen Arabic reports are unchanged. Entry 415 has one declared hamzah correction, سأل الوادي to سال الوادي, supported by both Arabic prints; the complete original remains available offline.

Historical print PDF pages 116–120 and modern print PDF pages 113–118 were visually inspected. Modern numbers 418–434 and English EPUB labels 1.8.410–1.8.426 were matched individually to their complete bodies. Each pinned EPUB record has exact source/record evidence. This local mapping is not a universal offset.

409 retains the selected led us wording, despite different printed wording; the placement of the prayer-and-bowing phrase is documented as a grammar question. 410 preserves both horse-racing routes and its closing participation statement without importing a compiler note absent from the selected report.

411 retains And Ibrahim said, the complete repeated carrying exchange, all four No answers, our sight and the final dirham. 412 retains I stood there, omitted by both English comparisons, and the singular departure. 413 preserves its question and the term lian without inserting a legal answer or extra participants. 414 keeps the selected pray for you wording and the narrator perspective change.

415 keeps the eyesight qualification, if Allah wills, until he had entered, the complete conversation, uncertainty in the man’s name, both face-of-Allah statements and the closing Ibn Shihab/al-Husayn confirmation omitted from the English EPUB. Its closing transmission remains visible and part of the complete narration script.

418 retains all three Arabic paragraphs, fourteen nights, the complete building account and both separately sourced verse lines. The two-sides English rendering of عضادتيه remains provisional with the door-post/support interpretation documented. No alternate verse or witness-only honorific is imported. 419 keeps the later-hearing note without inserting a speaker name: the two English comparisons and Fath al-Bari differ in their attribution.

416 retains as far as he could and all his affairs without a comparison gloss. 420 receives no additional kneeling/barrier detail. 421 adds no prayer-type explanation. 422 does not insert optional-prayer wording. 423 retains the dual honorific and complete warning. 424 preserves righteous servant—or righteous man instead of flattening the uncertainty or importing the Resurrection wording from 417.

Six original Arabic introductions remain separately browseable in chapters 46, 47, 48, 51, 53 and 54. A compiler definition missing from digital chapter 42 is supplied separately with two printed readings, exact pages, transcription policy and pending-review status. Its dual/plural vocalization is preserved. All chapter material stays outside daily numbered sessions and narration; English introductions remain pending.
remaining: 74 candidate Prayer reports (425–498), later chapter comparisons, English chapter introductions and independent Arabic/English/lexical/reference review remain. Full original source material is retained; unadmitted candidates are not reader content.
